text: Cheers for Lindsay Clancy. This was the extraordinary scene today as she arrived to court with hundreds of women wearing pink showing their support. Despite her saying she killed her three children in a moment of postpartum psychosis, as Anna McAuley reports, many are showing her sympathy. Right now, Lindsay Clancy is on trial for killing all three of her children. And over the past few weeks, I have received so many requests from you guys to cover this story. I was actually avoiding it because there is just so much going on here. But finally, I give up. So here we go. The most basic fact of this case is not really disputed. Lindsay Clancy killed her three children. And yet, a lot of people online are defending her, some are blaming her doctors, and some are even blaming her husband. So before we get into any of that, let's start from the beginning. What actually happened? Lindsay and Patrick Clancy lived in Duxbury, Massachusetts, with their three children, five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson, and eight-month-old Callan. Lindsay was a labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital while Patrick worked in tech. After Callan was born, Lindsay began struggling badly with her mental health. She was dealing with anxiety and depression, was prescribed multiple psychiatric medications, had talked about suicide, and reported unwanted thoughts about harming the children. And earlier that same month, she had spent five days at McLean Psychiatric Hospital. There are some very important details behind all of that, but for now, let's go to January 24th, 2023. According to Patrick, that was actually one of Lindsay's best days in months. He was working from home and Lindsay was with the children. Later that afternoon, Lindsay asked Patrick to pick up medicine for one of the kids from CVS, basically a pharmacy chain, and get takeout from a restaurant called 3V. At 5.10 pm, Lindsay called the restaurant and placed the order. At around 5.15 pm, Patrick left the house. Surveillance footage shows him inside CVS at 5.32 pm. A minute later, he called Lindsay to confirm which medicine to buy. She didn't answer, but called him back shortly afterwards. The call lasted about 14 seconds. Patrick testified that she sounded quiet, almost like she was busy, but nothing made him think something was seriously wrong. He bought the medicine, picked up the food, and returned home at around 6.09 pm. He had been gone for less than an hour. And during that time, Lindsay strangled all three of their children with exercise bands. She then cut her wrist and neck and jumped from a second-story bedroom window in an apparent attempt to kill herself. When Patrick came home, he immediately noticed how unusually quiet the house was. He called out for Lindsay and the kids. No answer. He went upstairs and found their bedroom door locked. When he unlocked it, he saw blood everywhere and an open window. He ran outside, found Lindsay badly injured on the ground, and called 911. Patrick asked her what she had done. She told him, I tried to kill myself. Then he asked where the children were. She said, in the basement. Once paramedics arrived to treat Lindsay, Patrick ran back inside, still on the phone with 911. Moments later, police officers outside heard him screaming from the basement. On the 911 call, he can be heard yelling, she killed the kids. Patrick found all three children with exercise bands around their necks and began trying to save them before emergency responders took over. Cora and Dawson were pronounced dead that night. Eight-month-old Callan still had a faint pulse and was rushed to Boston Children's Hospital, but he died three days later. Lindsay survived the fall but suffered a severe spinal cord injury and was left paralyzed from the waist down. And that brings us to the actual question of the center of this trial, not who killed the children. Both sides agree Lindsay did. The question is whether she was criminally responsible when she killed them. Her defense says she was suffering from severe mental illness, including postpartum psychosis. The prosecution says she was depressed but not psychotic and argues that she understood what she was doing and knew it was wrong. And to understand that argument, you have to understand what was happening to Lindsay in the months before the killings, because that is where this case gets much more complicated.
